title: Transformer-assisted survey identifies 87 previously unreported low-surface-brightness galaxies in Abell 194
summary: Transfer-learning transformer ensembles applied to deeper Hyper Suprime-Cam images of the Abell 194 cluster contributed to a vetted sample of 171 low-surface-brightness galaxies, including 87 reported as new discoveries. The models identified 159 sample members; Sérsic profile fitting and visual inspection were used to remove likely false positives, and the analysis characterized a subset of 28 ultra-diffuse galaxies. This is one paper-level survey result, not 87 separate catalog entries.
ai_technology: Ensembles of LSBG Detection Transformers (LSBG DETR) and LSBG Vision Transformers (LSBG ViT)
organization: National Centre for Nuclear Research, Poland; Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias; Stony Brook University; National Astronomical Observatory of Japan; collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: Transfer-learning transformer ensembles applied to deeper Hyper Suprime-Cam images of the Abell 194 cluster contributed to a vetted sample of 171 low-surface-brightness galaxies, including 87 reported as new discoveries.
evidence.unknown: The paper reports photometrically defined LSBGs and does not provide spectroscopic confirmation for every new object. The 87 are a sample-level count, not individually confirmed galaxy memberships; 12 of the 171 sample objects were found by visual inspection rather than the transformer models, so AI is not attributed to every sample detection.
evidence.ai_role: Applied models trained on Dark Energy Survey images to find low-surface-brightness structures in deeper HSC images from Abell 194 without fine-tuning; candidate masks were then assessed with Sérsic fits and human visual inspection.
